title: Sordland/Turn03/A_AddressProtestors
description:
President Anton and Serge Wolkner go to the Gasom front gate to address the crowd of protestors and union workers of the corporation. They are led and represented by Denis Stahler of the Communist Party of Sordland and Katarina Horten of the Labor Union. 

Anton gives a summary of the choices and discussions that took place in the event and based on how well received the response is can either leave via car or hunker down until an armored Presidential Guard convoy arrives.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“My fellow Sords, we are here today..."
entries.dialogueText: “My fellow Sords, we are here today not as adversaries, but as collaborators. Our purpose? To invest in Gasom, and ensure it invests in you.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Gus Manger stood to my right, his s..."
entries.dialogueText: Gus Manger stood to my right, his silhouette barely distinguishable from the monolithic edifice behind us.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Serge stood to my left, his eyes sc..."
entries.dialogueText: Serge stood to my left, his eyes scanning the crowd with the precision of a hawk.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The Gasom security had drawn their..."
entries.dialogueText: The Gasom security had drawn their weapons in anticipation, forming a bristling wall around the perimeter.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "My Presidential Guard, in stark con..."
entries.dialogueText: My Presidential Guard, in stark contrast, stood tall and unflinching at the entrance, shielding us from the sea of angry workers surrounding us.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The shouts of the crowd were deafen..."
entries.dialogueText: The shouts of the crowd were deafening, the hostility palpable. Stahler and Horten stood at the forefront with fire in their eyes.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "With a deep breath, I prepared to a..."
entries.dialogueText: With a deep breath, I prepared to address them.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Gus extended a megaphone towards me..."
entries.dialogueText: Gus extended a megaphone towards me.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As we stepped out of the towering f..."
entries.dialogueText: As we stepped out of the towering front gate of the Gasom facility, I immediately became aware of how tense the situation was.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“To the hard-working employees of G..."
entries.dialogueText: “To the hard-working employees of Gasom, we stand with you today. Our shared goal is simple: to demand improved living and working conditions for everyone.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good people of Narbel, we come her..."
entries.dialogueText: “Good people of Narbel, we come here today seeking understanding and progress. We aim to bridge the gap between Gasom and its employees.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Today my team and I are here to li..."
entries.dialogueText: “Today my team and I are here to listen and engage. We are here to ensure Gasom becomes a beacon of growth, fairness, and prosperity for all its workers.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We are not blind to your struggles..."
entries.dialogueText: “We are not blind to your struggles. We seek to acknowledge them, address them, and above all, improve them.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This is not a hollow promise, but..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is not a hollow promise, but a step towards a stronger and more balanced Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Remember, we are united by a commo..."
entries.dialogueText: “Remember, we are united by a common goal: A prosperous Gasom that cares for its workers. It's a fight we all must face together.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Let's turn this impasse into an op..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's turn this impasse into an opportunity -- a chance for real, impactful change. We are here to make that happen.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A group of figures emerged from the..."
entries.dialogueText: A group of figures emerged from the crowd, adorned in unmistakable scarlet attire. The Red Youth had arrived.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“My fellow Sords, our presence toda..."
entries.dialogueText: “My fellow Sords, our presence today is not a guarantee of instant change, but rather an effort to better understand the complexity of the issues at hand.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Good people of Narbel, we are here..."
entries.dialogueText: “Good people of Narbel, we are here not to placate you with false promises, but to honestly assess the reality and work towards practical solutions.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We recognize that words are not en..."
entries.dialogueText: “We recognize that words are not enough, and only through concrete action can we begin to address the challenges you face.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Today’s visit, let's be clear, doe..."
entries.dialogueText: “Today’s visit, let's be clear, does not mean all your problems will disappear overnight. It's an initial step to gauge the scope of the issues.”

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: "“Speeches and more speeches, from P..."
entries.dialogueText: “Speeches and more speeches, from President Rayne! But what exactly was decided today? We need more than pretty words; we need substance!”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: "“She's right, Mr. President. We nee..."
entries.dialogueText: “She's right, Mr. President. We need details. What's going to change for the workers?”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I realized this was no longer a mer..."
entries.dialogueText: I realized this was no longer a mere protest. It was a symbol of a broader, more potent struggle.

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: "“Empty words, Rayne! You've shown u..."
entries.dialogueText: “Empty words, Rayne! You've shown us nothing concrete today. We're fed up with your hollow rhetoric!”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: "“All talk and no action, isn't it,..."
entries.dialogueText: “All talk and no action, isn't it, Mr. President? How long must the workers wait for real change?”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Now hold on a moment. President Ra..."
entries.dialogueText: “Now hold on a moment. President Rayne is committed to bringing about real change. His actions and decisions demonstrate this clearly, even if it doesn't fit your narrative!”

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: "“Wasn't it your government that bai..."
entries.dialogueText: “Wasn't it your government that bailed out the elites while workers were left to suffer? Where was our bailout, Mr. President?”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Let's not forget your conspicuous..."
entries.dialogueText: "Let's not forget your conspicuous absence at Bernard Circas' funeral. Your silence spoke volumes. Do you endorse the killing of those who stand up for workers' rights?"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Is that so, Manger? All we've seen..."
entries.dialogueText: "Is that so, Manger? All we've seen are decisions that favor the likes of you and Ewald Alphonso, not the common workers!"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""It's not about narratives, Mr. Man..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's not about narratives, Mr. Manger. It's about ensuring a fair, dignified life for the working class. Something your policies have consistently failed to do."

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: ""Now, now, let's not get too heated..."
entries.dialogueText: "Now, now, let's not get too heated. We all know change doesn't happen overnight. President Rayne is doing what he can."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Time is a luxury we don't have, Mr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Time is a luxury we don't have, Mr. President. Each passing day is another day our workers suffer under the heel of inequality."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Oh, we've seen how much he can do,..."
entries.dialogueText: "Oh, we've seen how much he can do, Manger. A lot for you, President Alphonso and Gasom, nothing for the workers!"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Change might not happen overnight,..."
entries.dialogueText: "Change might not happen overnight, Mr. Manger, but it should at least happen! What we've seen so far is the same old corporate favoritism."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Quiet murmurs of discontent began t..."
entries.dialogueText: Quiet murmurs of discontent began to ripple through the crowd. The workers' faces seemed to turn even stonier.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Despite the sharp words exchanged,..."
entries.dialogueText: Despite the sharp words exchanged, the crowd remained eerily calm.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I could feel the tension growing. T..."
entries.dialogueText: I could feel the tension growing. The presence of our guards did little to reassure me.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "It seemed like they were waiting, t..."
entries.dialogueText: It seemed like they were waiting, their collective breath held in anticipation of something more.

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: "“Your boost to the police force? A..."
entries.dialogueText: “Your boost to the police force? A disaster! Inexperienced personnel are not only useless, they are dangerous. They're making the situation worse!”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""You label peaceful protestors as t..."
entries.dialogueText: "You label peaceful protestors as traitors? These are ordinary citizens expressing their discontent, not some foreign enemies."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The business bailout was a necessa..."
entries.dialogueText: “The business bailout was a necessary step to protect the livelihoods of millions of Sords. It was not a decision made lightly.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“My absence at Bernard Circas's fun..."
entries.dialogueText: “My absence at Bernard Circas's funeral was not an endorsement of his murder. It was a time of mourning, and political statements were uncalled for.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I have always valued the right to..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have always valued the right to peaceful protest. Any assertion otherwise is a misunderstanding.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The discussions with Gasom are an..."
entries.dialogueText: “The discussions with Gasom are an ongoing process, and I am committed to finding the best possible outcome for the workers of Narbel.”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""And what about the recent campaign..."
entries.dialogueText: "And what about the recent campaign finance bill, Mr. President? It's a direct attack on democracy, effectively silencing smaller parties like ours!"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Mr. President, we demand that you..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, we demand that you support the upcoming Worker's Rights Bill. The labor force of Sordland will be watching your next move closely!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“As a result of our negotiations, G..."
entries.dialogueText: “As a result of our negotiations, Gasom has committed to improving the living conditions for its workers. This includes providing private housing and ensuring access to healthcare and education.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Gasom has recognized the value of..."
entries.dialogueText: “Gasom has recognized the value of its blue-collar workers and agreed to increase their wages. These hardworking individuals are the backbone of their operations and deserve fair compensation.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I am pleased to announce that Gaso..."
entries.dialogueText: “I am pleased to announce that Gasom will play a crucial role in the recovery of Narbel. They have pledged a significant contribution to local charities.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I know it's hard to believe. But t..."
entries.dialogueText: “I know it's hard to believe. But today was a victory."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“A wage increase is not a mere poss..."
entries.dialogueText: “A wage increase is not a mere possibility, but a fact. This is a landmark moment.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“With this contribution, Gasom is s..."
entries.dialogueText: “With this contribution, Gasom is stepping up to play an essential part in the recovery and development of Narbel.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This is a vital step towards build..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is a vital step towards building a more resilient workforce.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This is a substantial step towards..."
entries.dialogueText: “This is a substantial step towards ensuring well-being and prosperity for all workers, not just Gasom's."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The worst-off will benefit under t..."
entries.dialogueText: “The worst-off will benefit under these new initiatives.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Our efforts have borne fruit. Gaso..."
entries.dialogueText: “Our efforts have borne fruit. Gasom will now provide better housing, healthcare, and education for every worker.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Through hard negotiations, we've s..."
entries.dialogueText: “Through hard negotiations, we've secured a commitment from Gasom to significantly better the lives of its employees. Upgraded housing, assured healthcare, and opportunities for education are now guaranteed.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“After much deliberation, Gasom has..."
entries.dialogueText: “After much deliberation, Gasom has agreed to increase the wages of the blue-collar workers on whose labor its success rests.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“In acknowledgment of their indispe..."
entries.dialogueText: “In acknowledgment of their indispensable workforce, Gasom has decided to raise the wages of its blue-collar workers.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I have exciting news: Gasom has pr..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have exciting news: Gasom has promised a substantial contribution to local charities, a move that will play a central role in the recovery efforts for Narbel."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Gasom's dedication to Narbel's rec..."
entries.dialogueText: “Gasom's dedication to Narbel's recovery has been cemented with their promise of a large contribution to local charities.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I must admit, we haven't been able..."
entries.dialogueText: “I must admit, we haven't been able to make as much progress with Gasom as we had hoped. But I remain committed to finding a solution.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Rest assured, we are in continuous..."
entries.dialogueText: “Rest assured, we are in continuous dialogue with Gasom. I remain steadfast in my pursuit of better conditions for Narbel's workers.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I understand your frustration. Be..."
entries.dialogueText: “I understand your frustration. Be assured, I will push harder in the negotiations. The well-being of Narbel's workers is my priority.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The journey may be challenging, bu..."
entries.dialogueText: “The journey may be challenging, but I remain dedicated. Our workers deserve better, and I won't rest until we achieve that.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A change came over the crowd. The a..."
entries.dialogueText: A change came over the crowd. The angry shouts were replaced with cries of disbelief, then joy.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The air suddenly felt somewhat ligh..."
entries.dialogueText: The air suddenly felt somewhat lighter. Murmurs of conversation started to percolate through the crowd, signs of animosity dwindling.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I could hear the crowd growing rest..."
entries.dialogueText: I could hear the crowd growing restless. They once again broke into discontented murmurs, punctuated by the occasional shout.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The crowd roared back to life. I co..."
entries.dialogueText: The crowd roared back to life. I could practically feel the raw anger emanating from them. My guards took a step forward.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The effort of this government will..."
entries.dialogueText: “The effort of this government will go down in history.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We have all achieved a victory tod..."
entries.dialogueText: “We have all achieved a victory today.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“This marks the beginning of a new..."
entries.dialogueText: “This marks the beginning of a new era for the city.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I would like to announce that I've..."
entries.dialogueText: “I would like to announce that I've personally donated a portion of my salary to the Alphonso Foundation. It's a small step, but one that I believe can help those struggling with homelessness and income inequality."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I have made the decision to donate..."
entries.dialogueText: “I have made the decision to donate part of my own income to the Alphonso Foundation. In a position of power, it's important to lead by example, isn't it? Together, we can make a difference.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You'll be pleased to know that I'v..."
entries.dialogueText: “You'll be pleased to know that I've allocated a portion of my rather substantial salary to the Alphonso Foundation. It's the least I can do, considering my privileged position.”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""At least you're not hiding your la..."
entries.dialogueText: "At least you're not hiding your lack of progress anymore. Mere determination won't solve the workers' problems. We need results."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""And until we get them, we will con..."
entries.dialogueText: "And until we get them, we will continue to fight!"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The undercurrent of unrest swelled,..."
entries.dialogueText: The undercurrent of unrest swelled, threatening to surge into a full-blown tempest. The previous calm seemed like a distant memory, an illusion shattered by the harsh reality of discontent.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“What if I told you I decided to gi..."
entries.dialogueText: “What if I told you I decided to give away a fraction of my salary to the Alphonso Foundation? Would that make you happy?"

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""Mr. President, it's no secret that..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, it's no secret that there was a significant divide during the party leadership campaign involving you and former President Alphonso."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The sight of them transported me ba..."
entries.dialogueText: The sight of them transported me back to my days among the Young Sords, when face-offs with those clad in crimson were frequent.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The sight of them triggered nostalg..."
entries.dialogueText: The sight of them triggered nostalgia, memories of days filled with protests and camaraderie during our time at university.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I saw a few officers with nervous f..."
entries.dialogueText: I saw a few officers with nervous faces, belying their inexperience. They stood at attention, visibly on edge.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Out of nowhere, a man lunged toward..."
entries.dialogueText: Out of nowhere, a man lunged towards me from the crowd.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The reporter jumped in."
entries.dialogueText: The reporter jumped in.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Denis, the focus here is not on na..."
entries.dialogueText: “Denis, the focus here is not on narratives or images but on real, tangible changes. It's a process, and we are on the right track.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I understand your skepticism, Deni..."
entries.dialogueText: “I understand your skepticism, Denis. But I assure you my administration is devoted to bringing about better conditions for our workers.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You're an academic and a lawyer, M..."
entries.dialogueText: “You're an academic and a lawyer, Mr. Stahler. What do you really know about the struggles of the working class?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You're right, Denis. The days of c..."
entries.dialogueText: “You're right, Denis. The days of corporate favoritism must come to an end. If not overnight, then soon.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Change may not come as quickly as..."
entries.dialogueText: “Change may not come as quickly as you want, Denis. But your claims of corporate favoritism don't reflect the complexity of the situation.”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Words, words, and more words, Pres..."
entries.dialogueText: "Words, words, and more words, President Rayne. What the workers need are actions, not promises."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Your words are compelling, Preside..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your words are compelling, President Rayne. But can they truly outweigh the years of corporate dominance?"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""I know that they deserve better th..."
entries.dialogueText: "I know that they deserve better than a president who puts corporate interests over human well-being."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Change is often slow and gradual...."
entries.dialogueText: “Change is often slow and gradual. Not all solutions are as immediate and straightforward as you make them out to be.”

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Your indifference is appalling, Pr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your indifference is appalling, President Rayne! The working class can't afford the luxury of time you're so fond of."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""We have had it with excuses, Presi..."
entries.dialogueText: "We have had it with excuses, President Rayne! The workers of Sordland need immediate solutions!"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Exactly, Denis. The working class..."
entries.dialogueText: "Exactly, Denis. The working class of Sordland is still waiting for those actions."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Your intentions sound noble, Presi..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your intentions sound noble, President Rayne. But intentions alone don't feed families or pay bills. We need concrete actions."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Attacking Mr. Stahler's personal b..."
entries.dialogueText: "Attacking Mr. Stahler's personal background accomplishes nothing, Mr. President. What do you have to say to the workers of this nation?"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Then what just happened in that bu..."
entries.dialogueText: "Then what just happened in that building, President Rayne? Did you advocate for Gasom's workers, or will its executives only be getting richer?"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Finally, Rayne, you acknowledge th..."
entries.dialogueText: "Finally, Rayne, you acknowledge the problem! But acknowledging is not enough. We need action."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""So, President Rayne agrees with De..."
entries.dialogueText: "So, President Rayne agrees with Denis! But will this realization actually result in action?"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""There are mothers in Narbel who ca..."
entries.dialogueText: "There are mothers in Narbel who cannot afford to feed their children. Where is the complexity in that?"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""It's clear from your lack of commi..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's clear from your lack of commitment to education that you don't fully comprehend the scope of the challenges faced by our workers' families."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Your neglect of our nation's healt..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your neglect of our nation's healthcare system will harm millions."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Furthermore, we want reform! Reduc..."
entries.dialogueText: "Furthermore, we want reform! Reduce the election threshold and change the constitution to make a more democratic and fairer nation!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The people of Sordland have electe..."
entries.dialogueText: "The people of Sordland have elected me to lead. I believe it's crucial to trust the government's judgement in these times of crisis."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I understand the concerns and frus..."
entries.dialogueText: "I understand the concerns and frustrations many of you have. Rest assured, we are here, we are listening, and we are committed to addressing these issues."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We must recognize that our country..."
entries.dialogueText: "We must recognize that our country can't solve all its problems at once. We are working hard and making progress, but our troubles won't simply vanish."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The campaign finance bill ensures..."
entries.dialogueText: "The campaign finance bill ensures fair funding for democratically elected parties. It's not an attack on democracy but a measure to safeguard it."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""While the increased police force m..."
entries.dialogueText: "While the increased police force may have its challenges, it's crucial for maintaining peace and order in our society. Their training and experience will improve over time."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""On healthcare and education, I hea..."
entries.dialogueText: "On healthcare and education, I hear your concerns. While these areas may not be our immediate focus, we are yet to finalize the government budget and are giving thoughtful consideration to those areas."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Suddenly, a reporter pushed through..."
entries.dialogueText: Suddenly, a reporter pushed through the crowd, brandishing a microphone towards me.

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""The locals of Narbel have suffered..."
entries.dialogueText: "The locals of Narbel have suffered under the impact of Gasom for years."

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""What concrete steps is Gasom going..."
entries.dialogueText: "What concrete steps is Gasom going to take for the benefit of the local community?"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Katarina and Denis raised their han..."
entries.dialogueText: Katarina and Denis raised their hands in a plea for calm, their words nearly lost amidst the turmoil.

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Private housing, healthcare, and e..."
entries.dialogueText: "Private housing, healthcare, and education? That's indeed a shift from the status quo, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""If these promises materialize, it..."
entries.dialogueText: "If these promises materialize, it could mean a significant improvement in the lives of our comrades at Gasom. This is a start, albeit late. Let's hope it's not mere lip service."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""While I commend this commitment to..."
entries.dialogueText: "While I commend this commitment to improve the lives of our Gasom workers, we can only hope this is not just another political gambit."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""So our blue-collar comrades are fi..."
entries.dialogueText: "So our blue-collar comrades are finally getting the attention they deserve, are they? I must admit, that's a step forward."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""An increase in wages, finally! It'..."
entries.dialogueText: "An increase in wages, finally! It's about time, Mr. President. While I appreciate this apparent commitment, let's not pat ourselves on the back just yet."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""But let's not forget, President Ra..."
entries.dialogueText: "But let's not forget, President Rayne, that this is only correcting a long-standing injustice. We will wait and see if these are empty promises or if you truly intend to uphold the rights of our working class."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Real success will be measured in t..."
entries.dialogueText: "Real success will be measured in the paychecks of the workers, not in words spoken here today."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Charitable contributions, Mr. Pres..."
entries.dialogueText: "Charitable contributions, Mr. President? Is that all Gasom can offer?"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""What we need, Mr. President, is no..."
entries.dialogueText: "What we need, Mr. President, is not a one-time act of charity, but a sustained commitment to improving the living conditions and wage disparity."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""While the effort is appreciated, t..."
entries.dialogueText: "While the effort is appreciated, these gestures do little to address the structural inequalities faced by the workers. We need systemic change, not charity."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Gasom's 'charity' must not be used..."
entries.dialogueText: "Gasom's 'charity' must not be used as a smokescreen to cover their ongoing exploitation."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""That's rich, Mr. President! Donati..."
entries.dialogueText: "That's rich, Mr. President! Donating a fraction of your salary while our people continue to suffer. How generous."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The Alphonso Foundation? More like..."
entries.dialogueText: "The Alphonso Foundation? More like the President's personal PR project. Let's not forget the true struggles of the Sordish people."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The police began reorganizing their..."
entries.dialogueText: The police began reorganizing their ranks, adopting defensive postures.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The past is the past. Personal dis..."
entries.dialogueText: "The past is the past. Personal disagreements have no place in matters of national importance. Our discussions were focused solely on what was best for Sordland."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We did have our disagreements, but..."
entries.dialogueText: "We did have our disagreements, but I won't allow personal matters to obstruct progress. We're both professional enough to separate politics from the welfare of the nation."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The rift between former President..."
entries.dialogueText: "The rift between former President Alphonso and myself did present obstacles in the negotiations. His reluctance to find common ground was a hurdle."

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""Could you shed some light on the p..."
entries.dialogueText: "Could you shed some light on the possible deal between the Sordish government and Gasom?"

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""Did this 'bad blood' influence you..."
entries.dialogueText: "Did this 'bad blood' influence your negotiations with Gasom?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“No comment.”"
entries.dialogueText: “No comment.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“To clarify, we tried our best to m..."
entries.dialogueText: “To clarify, we tried our best to mediate and negotiate a best possible outcome.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Gus stepped in."
entries.dialogueText: Gus stepped in.

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""What role does the Kingdom of Rizi..."
entries.dialogueText: "What role does the Kingdom of Rizia play in this arrangement?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""With all due respect to the Kingdo..."
entries.dialogueText: "With all due respect to the Kingdom, I believe Sordland knows whats best for Sordish companies. That's why our government is investing in Gasom alone."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Our nation will shoulder the inves..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our nation will shoulder the investment for Gasom. It's a bold step, but one that underscores our commitment to self-reliance and autonomy."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The government of Sordland has dec..."
entries.dialogueText: "The government of Sordland has decided to solely invest in Gasom. We believe this will lead to a direct positive impact on the citizens of Sordland."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""In a show of international coopera..."
entries.dialogueText: "In a show of international cooperation, Sordland and Rizia will jointly invest in Gasom."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We are sharing the costs and stake..."
entries.dialogueText: "We are sharing the costs and stakes with Rizia. This way, we're reducing financial pressure and fostering international relationships."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Sordland is renewing its ties with..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sordland is renewing its ties with the Kingdom of Rizia. Together, we will provide the funding that Gasom and its workers need."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Our government has chosen not to i..."
entries.dialogueText: "Our government has chosen not to invest at this time. We believe Rizia is capable of handling the investment, giving us the opportunity to focus our resources on other pressing issues."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Rizia has invested in Sordland bef..."
entries.dialogueText: "Rizia has invested in Sordland before, and they will do it once again. I have faith in the Kingdom and its vision for Gasom."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""At this time, we won't be investin..."
entries.dialogueText: "At this time, we won't be investing in Gasom. This decision isn't made lightly, but we're confident Rizia can handle the situation."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Encouraging, President Rayne. As l..."
entries.dialogueText: "Encouraging, President Rayne. As long as your government's drive to recoup your investment doesn't take precedent over Gasom's struggling labor force."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""A surprising but potentially promi..."
entries.dialogueText: "A surprising but potentially promising decision, Mr. President. Let's hope your confidence isn't misplaced."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""We will be watching this co-invest..."
entries.dialogueText: "We will be watching this co-investment closely. Your government will be responsible for keeping its partner's worst tendencies in check."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""A partnership with Rizia? You are..."
entries.dialogueText: "A partnership with Rizia? You are aware of the monarchy's history of stamping out disagreements with brute force."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Relinquishing control to a monarch..."
entries.dialogueText: "Relinquishing control to a monarchy!? You are aware of Rizia's history of stamping out disagreements with brute force."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""So, you're putting the fate of our..."
entries.dialogueText: "So, you're putting the fate of our workers in the King of Rizia's hands? That's a dangerous game you're playing, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You speak of double standards and..."
entries.dialogueText: "You speak of double standards and yet fail to understand the complexities of governance! It's easy to criticize from the sidelines, but real change requires pragmatism, not idealism."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You claim to advocate for the work..."
entries.dialogueText: "You claim to advocate for the workers, yet undermine our efforts to better their condition. Shouldn't you be supporting the initiatives we've fought for, instead of spreading discontent?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The utopia you dream of won't mate..."
entries.dialogueText: "The utopia you dream of won't materialize by mere rhetoric or by attacking those striving for change. It requires understanding the political and economic landscape and making informed decisions."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Let's all remember that we're here..."
entries.dialogueText: "Let's all remember that we're here for the same reason -- to better the lives of our citizens. Let's not allow our differences to blind us to our common goals."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""The path to progress is challengin..."
entries.dialogueText: "The path to progress is challenging and fraught with disagreement, but we must not let this divide us."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I understand your frustrations and..."
entries.dialogueText: "I understand your frustrations and the urge to voice your concerns. However, let's keep our discourse respectful and constructive."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""I recommend that we expedite your..."
entries.dialogueText: "I recommend that we expedite your departure. We must prioritize your safety."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""It might be a good time to make ou..."
entries.dialogueText: "It might be a good time to make our way to the convoy, before any potential escalation."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""It may be best to conclude your ad..."
entries.dialogueText: "It may be best to conclude your address and proceed to the vehicle."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Close by, I noticed a terse exchang..."
entries.dialogueText: Close by, I noticed a terse exchange between a security officer from Gasom and a member of the Presidential Guard.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Serge craned his neck, his face dee..."
entries.dialogueText: Serge craned his neck, his face deep in concentration as he listened to their whispers.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Nearby, a quick, hushed conversatio..."
entries.dialogueText: Nearby, a quick, hushed conversation was being had between a Gasom security officer and a Presidential Guard. I followed their eyes to the protestors. Some had calmed down; others still seemed agitated.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Serge craned his neck, his face dee..."
entries.dialogueText: Serge craned his neck, his face deep in concentration as he listened to their whispers.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Nearby, a Gasom security officer an..."
entries.dialogueText: Nearby, a Gasom security officer and a Presidential Guard member were conversing in hushed tones.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I saw them glance over the crowd, n..."
entries.dialogueText: I saw them glance over the crowd, now calmer but still restless.

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: ""I'll stay back and handle things h..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'll stay back and handle things here. You should head to safety."

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: ""Mr. President, I'll stay on to fur..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, I'll stay on to further address the crowd. The mood is still tense, but I think I can manage. You should get on your way."

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: ""I'll remain here, Mr. President. T..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'll remain here, Mr. President. The crowd seems calmer now, and I believe I can answer their queries and maintain the peace. You should go ahead."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""You can't even face your own peopl..."
entries.dialogueText: "You can't even face your own people, can you, Mr. President? We expected better."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Leaving so soon, Rayne? I guess yo..."
entries.dialogueText: "Leaving so soon, Rayne? I guess you know when you've been defeated."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""We will hold you accountable to yo..."
entries.dialogueText: "We will hold you accountable to your promises. The troubles of the laborers continue and our union is here to solve them."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""I'm impressed you even came out to..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm impressed you even came out to speak to us, President Rayne. Most wouldn't. However, this conversation isn't over yet."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Mr. President, thank you for your..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, thank you for your willingness to address us. Let's continue these important conversations moving forward."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""You've shown courage today. We'll..."
entries.dialogueText: "You've shown courage today. We'll see if your actions match your words. Until next time."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Thank you for looking out for me,..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thank you for looking out for me, Serge. Let's get out of here."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Are you sure? Won't running away f..."
entries.dialogueText: "Are you sure? Won't running away from this only make the protestors angrier?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I agree, Serge. Tensions can rise..."
entries.dialogueText: "I agree, Serge. Tensions can rise quickly in such environments. It's better we make our exit now."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Are you sure? Won't running away f..."
entries.dialogueText: "Are you sure? Won't running away from this only make the protestors angrier?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You're absolutely right, Serge. Le..."
entries.dialogueText: "You're absolutely right, Serge. Let's not stay here any longer than necessary."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Are you sure? Won't running away f..."
entries.dialogueText: "Are you sure? Won't running away from this only make the protestors angrier?"

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""Mr. President, the situation is gr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, the situation is growing increasingly volatile."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""Sir, the crowd is no longer entire..."
entries.dialogueText: "Sir, the crowd is no longer entirely hostile, but there's still an undercurrent of tension."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""President Rayne, while the crowd a..."
entries.dialogueText: "President Rayne, while the crowd appears somewhat subdued, I would advise we exercise caution."

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""Can you clarify the current status..."
entries.dialogueText: "Can you clarify the current status of your personal relationship with Ewa-"

entries.speaker: Reporter
entries.title: Reporter: ""One final question, what is your t..."
entries.dialogueText: "One final question, what is your true personal relationship with Ew-"

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I reached out my hand, and Katarina..."
entries.dialogueText: I reached out my hand, and Katarina shook it with a smile. Denis followed suit.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I reached out my hand, and Katarina..."
entries.dialogueText: I reached out my hand, and Katarina reluctantly shook it. Denis followed suit.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""No further comments.""
entries.dialogueText: "No further comments."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Serge left my dazed attacker on the..."
entries.dialogueText: Serge left my dazed attacker on the ground and turned to the guards with a look of authority I'd never seen before.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "His voice carried over the screams..."
entries.dialogueText: His voice carried over the screams of the crowd. The guards tightened their circle around me, hurriedly pushing me towards the safety of the convoy.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Police and security forces rushed i..."
entries.dialogueText: Police and security forces rushed into the melee, swinging batons with indiscriminate ferocity. The Red Youth rushed at them head-on.

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Stop the cops! This isn't going to..."
entries.dialogueText: "Stop the cops! This isn't going to help!"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Everyone, remain calm!""
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone, remain calm!"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Their screams receded into the back..."
entries.dialogueText: Their screams receded into the background as we left the chaotic scene behind.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Give him hell, Serge!""
entries.dialogueText: "Give him hell, Serge!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Let's get out of here!""
entries.dialogueText: "Let's get out of here!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Everyone calm down!""
entries.dialogueText: "Everyone calm down!"

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: ""Back off! You're only making thing..."
entries.dialogueText: "Back off! You're only making things worse!"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The staff and I were swiftly escort..."
entries.dialogueText: The staff and I were swiftly escorted into the convoy. The protestors and police scattered as our vehicles plowed through the crowd.

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""Into the car, Mr. President! We ar..."
entries.dialogueText: "Into the car, Mr. President! We are leaving NOW!"

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Before I could react, Serge sprang..."
entries.dialogueText: Before I could react, Serge sprang in front of me. He swiftly tackled the man to the ground and pinned his hands behind his back.

entries.speaker: Player_Italic
entries.title: Player_Italic: "I froze in panic."
entries.dialogueText: I froze in panic.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The nervous officers I'd seen befor..."
entries.dialogueText: The nervous officers I'd seen before now looked completely overwhelmed. They lashed out left and right, hitting protestors, Red Youth members and their own colleagues alike.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Thanks to both of you.""
entries.dialogueText: "Thanks to both of you."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""No more questions, please.""
entries.dialogueText: "No more questions, please."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""Mr. President, if you could please..."
entries.dialogueText: "Mr. President, if you could please proceed to the vehicle."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Yes, the dialogue has only started..."
entries.dialogueText: "Yes, the dialogue has only started. I assure you both, my commitment to progress and change is unwavering."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Indeed, accountability is the corn..."
entries.dialogueText: "Indeed, accountability is the cornerstone of democracy. As your president, I understand that responsibility."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Most wouldn't come out because mos..."
entries.dialogueText: "Most wouldn't come out because most fear facing the truth. As for the conversation, it's always been going on."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""My job is to listen and act. As fo..."
entries.dialogueText: "My job is to listen and act. As for accountability, isn't that what all governments should be held to? You have my word."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Denis, Katarina, I look forward to..."
entries.dialogueText: "Denis, Katarina, I look forward to our continuing conversations."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""This is a marathon, not a sprint.""
entries.dialogueText: "This is a marathon, not a sprint."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""As an old Red Youth member, I can..."
entries.dialogueText: "As an old Red Youth member, I can personally say that the work you do is of utmost importance. Thank you."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Almost immediately, the remaining t..."
entries.dialogueText: Almost immediately, the remaining tension in the crowd dissipated. A few workers nearby broke into scattered applause.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "A flutter of whispers rippled throu..."
entries.dialogueText: A flutter of whispers rippled through the sea of onlookers, their eyes darting back and forth between us in surprise. A few broke into scattered applause.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Their collective gaze bore into me,..."
entries.dialogueText: Their collective gaze bore into me, awaiting my words.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "I turned to the crowd one last time..."
entries.dialogueText: I turned to the crowd one last time. In their eyes, I saw both flashes of anger and glimmers of hope.

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""We have shown courage together. No..."
entries.dialogueText: "We have shown courage together. Now we will hold you accountable to your promises. The troubles of the laborers are not over, and neither is the work of our union."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As I readied myself to leave, I tur..."
entries.dialogueText: As I readied myself to leave, I turned back to Katarina and Denis a last time.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The initially hesitant clapping gre..."
entries.dialogueText: The initially hesitant clapping grew louder, and jubilant cheers and whistles filled the air. I saw the Red Youth members standing at the edge of the crowd with their arms folded, a hint of approval in their eyes.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Together, we can ensure a prospero..."
entries.dialogueText: "Together, we can ensure a prosperous future for Sordland."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Serge opened the door of the car an..."
entries.dialogueText: Serge opened the door of the car and I lowered myself into the seat. The door closed behind me with a thud, sealing off the external noise.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The crowd began to disperse, the in..."
entries.dialogueText: The crowd began to disperse, the individuals breaking away to let our convoy through. The guards took their position nonetheless, forming a human barrier around the vehicle.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The engine purred to life, and we b..."
entries.dialogueText: The engine purred to life, and we began to move.

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""I had no doubt about your capabili..."
entries.dialogueText: "I had no doubt about your capability to handle this, President Rayne. Still, I was worried for your safety."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""I'm glad we are safely on our way,..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm glad we are safely on our way, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "As we started moving, some disgrunt..."
entries.dialogueText: As we started moving, some disgruntled protestors rushed towards us. I could hear shouts and jeers as their fists pounded against the glass windows.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The guards sprang into action, push..."
entries.dialogueText: The guards sprang into action, pushing back the unruly crowd.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "It was a tense few moments before t..."
entries.dialogueText: It was a tense few moments before the convoy was able to navigate away from the tumult.

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Thanks for your concern, Serge. It..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thanks for your concern, Serge. It was tense, but knowing you and the team were there made all the difference."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Serge, in this role, danger comes..."
entries.dialogueText: "Serge, in this role, danger comes with the territory. But your concern is appreciated."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Don't forget, a President has to f..."
entries.dialogueText: "Don't forget, a President has to face these situations head-on."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Thank you, Serge. I don't know wha..."
entries.dialogueText: "Thank you, Serge. I don't know what I'd do without you."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Agreed, Serge. A job well done by..."
entries.dialogueText: "Agreed, Serge. A job well done by you and the team."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""A little excitement to keep us on..."
entries.dialogueText: "A little excitement to keep us on our toes, wasn't it?"

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""We're here to serve and protect, M..."
entries.dialogueText: "We're here to serve and protect, Mr. President. It's a duty we don't take lightly."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""It's not just part of the job, sir..."
entries.dialogueText: "It's not just part of the job, sir. It's a matter of personal commitment."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""You're right, sir. It's part of th..."
entries.dialogueText: "You're right, sir. It's part of the job, after all."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""I'm merely doing my job, Mr. Presi..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm merely doing my job, Mr. President. Ensuring your safety is my top priority."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""We appreciate your acknowledgement..."
entries.dialogueText: "We appreciate your acknowledgement, Mr. President. It's our duty and honor."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: ""That's one way to look at it, Mr...."
entries.dialogueText: "That's one way to look at it, Mr. President. Keeps the job interesting, to say the least."

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The echoing voices of the protester..."
entries.dialogueText: The echoing voices of the protesters gradually subsided as we retreated from the scene and left Narbel behind.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Eventually, all fell silent as they..."
entries.dialogueText: Eventually, all fell silent as they waited for Denis and Katarina to respond.

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: ""Serge is right, Mr. President. The..."
entries.dialogueText: "Serge is right, Mr. President. The crowd won't get any calmer if you stick around. You've got to get to safety."

entries.speaker: Serge Wolkner
entries.title: Serge Wolkner: "<shout>""PROTECT THE PRESIDENT!"</s..."
entries.dialogueText: <shout>""PROTECT THE PRESIDENT!"</shout>

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Before any of you do anything too..."
entries.dialogueText: "Before any of you do anything too rash, I want you to take a good look around you."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You are surrounded by police and a..."
entries.dialogueText: "You are surrounded by police and armed guards. Realistically, what do you hope to accomplish here?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""You cannot rise up against the Pre..."
entries.dialogueText: "You cannot rise up against the President of Sordland without facing consequences."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""We are all brothers and sisters in..."
entries.dialogueText: "We are all brothers and sisters in the struggle against greed and exploitation. We must not let ourselves become divided."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""You're going to jump directly to t..."
entries.dialogueText: "You're going to jump directly to threatening us, President Rayne? Whatever happened to the right to peaceful protest?"

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: "“This only proves that we are right..."
entries.dialogueText: “This only proves that we are right to stand here today. We will not budge until you commit to real change."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Divided? You're the one walking ou..."
entries.dialogueText: "Divided? You're the one walking out of Gasom headquarters surrounded by armed guards."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""How dare you speak that way to you..."
entries.dialogueText: "How dare you speak that way to your president! You ingrates have no idea how much I have sacrificed for this country."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I..."
entries.dialogueText: “See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I'm on your side. You can stop whining now."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I..."
entries.dialogueText: “See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I'm on your side. You can stop whining now."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I..."
entries.dialogueText: “See, Mr. Stahler and Ms. Horten? I'm on your side. You can stop whining now."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I'm not going to dignify that with..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'm not going to dignify that with a response. Gasom has done so much for this shithole region, and this is how you people repay it?"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Honestly, these workers are lucky..."
entries.dialogueText: "Honestly, these workers are lucky to even have jobs. They shouldn't get greedy."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""I'm warning you all. Back off now,..."
entries.dialogueText: "I'm warning you all. Back off now, or there *will* be consequences."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""Why don't you talk to an actual Ga..."
entries.dialogueText: "Why don't you talk to an actual Gasom employee, Madam Reporter? They'll tell you how grateful they are to work for the best company in Sordland."

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""Your arrogance is unbelievable, Mr..."
entries.dialogueText: "Your arrogance is unbelievable, Mr. President."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""Clearly, we are past the time for..."
entries.dialogueText: "Clearly, we are past the time for reasonable discussion. We must fight for what we believe in!"

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""What the hell are you still doing..."
entries.dialogueText: "What the hell are you still doing here, lady? Can't you see it's about to get ugly?"

entries.speaker: Denis Stahler
entries.title: Denis Stahler: ""The sight of the common people spe..."
entries.dialogueText: "The sight of the common people speaking truth to power is anything but 'ugly', Rayne."

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: ""That's confidential, ma'am.""
entries.dialogueText: "That's confidential, ma'am."

entries.speaker: Katarina Horten
entries.title: Katarina Horten: ""I see. The President won't divulge..."
entries.dialogueText: "I see. The President won't divulge any information about his closed-door dealings."
